question: What is a Type A adverse drug reaction?

options.B: It only occurs through immune mechanisms
options.C: It is rare and highly unpredictable
options.D: It is completely unrelated to dosage

explanation: Type A reactions happen because of the normal pharmacological action of a drug. They are predictable and happen more when the dose is higher. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h1)

question: A patient takes a normal dose of a drug and suddenly gets an unexpected, severe allergic rash. What type of reaction is this?
explanation: Type B reactions are bizarre, unpredictable, and do not depend on how much of the drug was given. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h1)

question: What happens in a Type E adverse drug reaction?

options.B: Long-term organ damage from chronic use
options.D: Withdrawal symptoms after stopping a drug

explanation: Type E reactions refer to withdrawal or rebound effects that occur when a medication is stopped suddenly. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h2)

question: A patient develops kidney damage after taking pain relievers for many years. Which reaction type is this?
explanation: Type C reactions are linked to long-term, continuous use of a medication over a long period. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h2)

question: Which sign suggests that a drug is suppressing the bone marrow?
explanation: Bone marrow suppression lowers blood platelets and clotting factors, leading to easy bruising and bleeding. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h3)

question: Why are adverse drug reactions sometimes mistaken for new illnesses?

options.A: Patients refuse to mention taking medications
options.B: They mimic common natural disease symptoms
options.C: Laboratory tests cannot detect drug metabolites
options.D: They always present with high fever first

explanation: Signs like upset stomach or confusion look like normal sickness, so healthcare workers can mistake them for a new disease. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h3)

question: What do we call the use of five or more medications by a single patient at the same time?
explanation: Polypharmacy means taking many drugs at once, which increases the chance of bad drug interactions. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h4)

question: Why is an elderly patient with reduced kidney function at a higher risk for adverse drug reactions?

options.A: Older adults always take too many herbal remedies
options.B: Drugs and metabolites are cleared much slower
options.C: Hepatic enzymes completely stop functioning with age

explanation: When kidneys work more slowly, drugs stay in the body longer and can build up to harmful levels. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h4)

question: What is the first thing a nurse should do when a severe adverse drug reaction happens?

options.D: Double the next scheduled drug dose

explanation: Stopping the drug right away prevents further harm and is the most important first step. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h5)

question: A patient has severe anaphylaxis after an antibiotic infusion. Which drug should be given immediately?
explanation: Epinephrine is the emergency treatment for anaphylaxis because it opens the airways and stabilizes blood pressure. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h5)

question: Which Nigerian agency collects reports on adverse drug reactions?
explanation: NAFDAC runs the National Pharmacovigilance Centre, which tracks drug safety and adverse reactions in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h6)

question: Why is it important to keep reporting adverse drug reactions even after a drug is approved and sold?

options.A: Pre-market trials cannot catch every rare or long-term reaction
options.B: It prevents patients from developing any type of drug tolerance
options.C: It guarantees that pharmaceutical companies will lower drug prices
options.D: It replaces the need for nurses to take patient allergy histories

explanation: Clinical trials test drugs on a small group of people, so monitoring after release helps find rare or long-term side effects. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h6)
